proof_summary: Writing the numerator and denominator as \(N_m,D_m\), the proof derives \(v_p(N_m)=\sum_{i\ge1}\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor^2\) and \(v_p(D_m)=\sum_{i\ge1}\sum_{r\le\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor}r\lfloor\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor/r\rfloor\); the bound \(\sum_{r\le M}r\lfloor M/r\rfloor\le M^2\) also gives \(D_m\mid N_m\), so the quotient valuation is their difference. For \(0\le k<p\), every \(i\ge1\) satisfies \(\lfloor(np+k)/p^i\rfloor=\lfloor np/p^i\rfloor\), making both valuation formulas—and hence their difference—unchanged.
